findings.current: “For some reason, everyone I meet always says that. Even though I’ve never once seen what the Fire King actually looks like.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the subject of the second sentence from the people Jin meets to Jin himself, falsely stating that Jin has never seen the Fire King.
findings.rationale: 본 적 없으면서 describes the people who repeatedly compare Jin to the Fire King, not Jin, who is the Fire King’s Disciple.
findings.replacement: “Funny how everyone I meet says that when none of them have ever even seen the Fire King’s face.”
findings.source: “이상하게 만나는 놈들마다 꼭 저 소리 하더라. 실제로는 화왕이 누구인지 얼굴 한번 본 적 없으면서.”

findings.current: “Old man! Can’t you keep your mouth shut?”
findings.defect: 노옴 is an elongated form of 놈, an insult aimed at Jin, not an address meaning “old man.” The draft therefore changes the addressee’s identity.
findings.rationale: Black Hand is angrily insulting Jin after Jin taunts both opponents; he is not addressing the slender old man.

findings.current:
“Why are you suddenly talking like some old-fashioned gentleman and spouting nonsense? A moment ago, you told one of us to sit out so you could face us in turn.”

“One of us? Did I say that?”
findings.defect: The draft removes 놈, the insulting noun Jin immediately pretends to be shocked by, breaking the register-shift joke.
findings.rationale: Jin’s mock-politeness depends on selectively objecting to his own earlier use of 놈 while pretending not to remember it.
findings.replacement:
“Why are you suddenly talking like some old-fashioned gentleman and spouting nonsense? A moment ago, you said you’d face us one at a time and told one bastard to stay out of it.”

“‘Bastard’? Did I say that?”
findings.source:
“갑자기 웬 하오체에 헛소리냐. 심지어 조금 전에는 차례대로 상대할 테니 한 놈은 빠져 있으라고 했으면서.”

“놈? 놈이요? 제가 그랬습니까?”

findings.current: “Fuck you. At least get fooled out of respect for the effort I put in.”
findings.defect: “Get fooled” is unnatural and loses the indulgent force of 속아 주지: Jin is asking the old man to play along and pretend to fall for it as a favor.
findings.rationale: The benefactive 주다 makes this a demand that the old man humor Jin, which drives the deadpan exchange that follows.
findings.replacement: “You fucking bastard. Then at least pretend to fall for it out of respect for the effort.”
findings.source: “시벌 새끼. 그럼 정성을 봐서라도 속아 주지.”

findings.current: “……Your tongue is far too short. I’m sure you were calling me Senior just a moment ago.”
findings.defect: The literal rendering of 혀가 짧다 is opaque in English and fails to convey that Jin’s speech abruptly became much less respectful.
findings.rationale: The old man is commenting on Jin’s sudden collapse from elaborate deference into insulting casual speech, not the physical length of his tongue.
findings.replacement: “……That tongue of yours got awfully rude, awfully fast. I could’ve sworn I was ‘Senior’ just a moment ago.”
findings.source: “……혀가 짧아도 너무 짧군. 분명 조금 전까진 노선배였던 것 같은데.”

findings.current: “For now, they are being kept somewhere safe. But once Her Majesty the Demon Empress returns, the pair of them will meet their end.”
findings.defect: “Somewhere safe” presents the captives as protected and removes the captor’s sarcastically courteous 곱게 모셔 두었지, while “the pair of them” also softens the contemptuous 연놈들.
findings.rationale: Black Hand mockingly describes imprisoning Heugung and Yohi as treating them like honored guests, then contemptuously threatens their tenacious lives.
findings.replacement: “For now, we have those two tucked away nice and comfortably. But once Her Majesty the Demon Empress returns, those bastards’ stubborn hold on life will end.”
findings.source: “우선은 곱게 모셔 두었지. 마후(魔后)께서 돌아오시면 그 연놈들의 질긴 명줄도 끝장이겠지만.”

findings.current: “Thanks for the great information. So the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that bitch—isn’t here. And the two of them are still in one piece.”
findings.defect: The stiff “great information” loses Jin’s gleefully crude slang, and “that bitch” softens the stronger 썅년.
findings.rationale: Jin abruptly drops into coarse, triumphant speech after tricking the enemy into confirming all three useful facts.
findings.replacement: “Thanks for the fucking useful intel. So the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that fucking bitch—isn’t here. And those two are still in one piece.”
findings.source: “개꿀 정보 고맙다. 일단 남천마후, 그 썅년은 여기에 없다는 소리네. 두 사람도 멀쩡하고.”

findings.current: “Then why did you two come together? Were you scared you’d get your ass kicked by a kid, so you brought your big brother along?”
findings.defect: The established kinship term 형 is flattened to “big brother,” losing the specifically junior-to-senior male hierarchy Jin is using to mock Black Hand.
findings.rationale: Jin sarcastically casts the colder senior fighter as Black Hand’s hyung; the relationship hierarchy is the point of the taunt.
findings.replacement: “Then why did you two come together? Were you scared a kid would kick your ass, so you brought your hyung?”
findings.source: “근데 왜 둘이 손잡고 왔니. 어린놈한테 줘 터질까 봐 쫄려서 형 데려온 거야?”

findings.current: The pair of twin wheels left the old man’s hand and came flying at us, tearing the air to shreds.
findings.defect: “Pair of twin wheels” is redundant, and “at us” supplies a plural target that the source leaves unstated.
findings.rationale: 두 자루의 쌍륜 identifies two matching wheel-shaped weapons; the sentence need not add a target beyond their incoming motion.
findings.replacement: The twin wheels flew from the old man’s hand, tearing through the air.
findings.source: 노인의 손을 떠난 두 자루의 쌍륜(雙輪)이, 공간을 찢어발기며 날아들었다.

findings.current: Their Pavilion Master, whose whereabouts and situation they knew nothing about by now.
findings.defect: “Whose whereabouts and situation they knew nothing about” is awkward and turns the concrete uncertainty about where Jin is and what he is doing into an abstract “situation.”
findings.rationale: 어디에서 무엇을 하고 있을지 directly expresses uncertainty about Jin’s present location and actions.
findings.replacement: Their Pavilion Master, though they had no idea where he was or what he might be doing now.
findings.source: 지금쯤 어디에서 무엇을 하고 있을지 모르는 자신들의 각주를.

summary: Two critical mistranslations alter a speaker’s subject and an insult; several additional findings concern lost register shifts, sarcasm, kinship, profanity, and localized English.
